missing_attribution: stage 1 (placed): no record of a goal that nothing ever detected, so 'never discovered' is counted against the configured num_goals, not against a log
stage 3 (delivered): no per-recipient loss record; attempts = arrived + lost closes per send, but which robot was left uninformed is unrecoverable
stage 4 (robot knew): belief writes are not an event type; the only per-(goal, robot) record is a transcript deliver row, and three non-message channels also write belief

stage 6 (arrived) and 7 (started work): no event type; both are proxies from fingerprint-changed progress rows, so they can postdate or predate each other (one hop mean in this file is negative for exactly that reason)

no archived run has live search, a non-trivial channel and per-goal execution attribution at once: the deployed runs are lossless, the lossy runs replay detections, and the isolated runs switch the environment's own sensing off
not_claimed: no bucket in this file is an intervention's causal gain: the deployed-path information bucket is reported as not attributable rather than as zero
arm-to-arm differences within a path are designed contrasts on shared scenarios; cross-path differences (a P1 rate against a P3 rate, for example) are not
the setting contrast compares identical transmission ledgers with the sensing bypass toggled, which measures the value of the environment's own sensing, not the value of any communication policy
nothing here reopens the learning question or proposes a change to a production default

P2_deployed_replayed_search.label: deployed path, replayed detections (joint_eval pilot)
P2_deployed_replayed_search.pairing: arms share the seed and the frozen detection stream; channel adds nothing
P2_deployed_replayed_search.search_backend: detections replayed from a frozen stream: the search stage is inherited from the recording run, not measured here

P3_isolated_budgeted_comm.label: isolated path, hard 29 300 B budget (task-pressure layers)
P3_isolated_budgeted_comm.pairing: arms share the seed; the channel is deterministic, so a per-stream pair is an exact match on everything except the send decisions
P3_isolated_budgeted_comm.search_backend: replayed detections, isolated (gossip_interval 100000), 29 300 B budget, policy_owned_timing

P4_lossy_confirmation.label: deployed and isolated lossy channels (S3 rule confirmation)
P4_lossy_confirmation.note: the round's own aggregate already carries per-arm discovered / on-time / expired / unresolved counts and the detection-to-assignment, -work and -completion latencies over 1 000 episodes each; re-deriving 1.65 GB of lifecycle logs would add cost and a second definition of the same quantity, so this round reads the aggregate and spot-checks the transcripts instead
P4_lossy_confirmation.pairing: the forward-loss stream is consumed per episode, so two arms that send different things draw different channel outcomes: same scenario, not common random numbers
P4_lossy_confirmation.search_backend: replayed detections on 200 fresh streams; only normal-lossy keeps line-of-sight refresh and gossip on
